arxiv-2212-13351.creator: Layton A. Hall 1 , Abbas Shiri 1 , and Ayman F. Abouraddy 1,
arxiv-2212-13351.description: Abstract Resonant field enhancement in optical cavities is provided over only narrow linewidths and for specific spatial modes. Consequently, spectrally restrictive planar Fabry-Pérot cavities have not contributed to date to white-light imaging, which necessitates a highly multimoded broadband field to satisfy the resonance condition.

arxiv-2312-12511.title: Stellar Flares Are Far-Ultraviolet Luminous Journal: MNRAS
arxiv-2312-12511.creator: Vera L. Berger, Jason T. Hinkle, Michael A. Tucker, Benjamin J. Shappee, Jennifer L. van Saders, Daniel Huber, Jeffrey W. Reep, Xudong Sun (孙旭东), Kai E. Yang (杨凯)
arxiv-2312-12511.description: Abstract We identify 182 flares on 158 stars within 100 pc of the Sun in both the near-ultraviolet (NUV: 1750 − 2750 1750-2750 Å) and far-ultraviolet (FUV: 1350 − 1750 1350-1750 Å) using high-cadence light curves from the Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) . Ultraviolet (UV) emission from stellar flares plays a crucial role in determining the habitability of exoplanetary systems.

arxiv-2401-12552.title: Network based Approach Estimating COVID-19 Spread Patterns
arxiv-2401-12552.creator: Jiarui Dong, Guanghao Ran
arxiv-2401-12552.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jiarui Dong, Guanghao Ran. In this study, we construct a series of evolving epidemic networks by measuring the correlations of daily COVID-19 cases time series among 3,105 counties in the United States. Remarkably, through quantitative analysis of the spatial distribution of these entities in different networks, we identify four typical patterns of COVID-19 transmission in the United States from March 2020 to February 2023. The onsets and wanes of these patterns are closely associated with significant events in the COVID-19 timeline.

arxiv-2402-07489.title: Network mechanism for generating genuinely correlative Gaussian states
arxiv-2402-07489.creator: Zhaofang Bai, Shuanping Du
arxiv-2402-07489.description: Abstract Generating a long-distance quantum state with genuine quantum correlation (GQC) is one of the most essential functions of quantum networks to support quantum communication. Here, we pro- vide a deterministic scheme for generating multimode Gaussian states with certain GQC (including genuine entanglement). Efficient algorithms of generating multimode states are also proposed.

arxiv-2406-06943.title: Fault + + Probe : A Generic Rowhammer-based Bit Recovery Attack
arxiv-2406-06943.creator: Kemal Derya, M. Caner Tol, and Berk Sunar
arxiv-2406-06943.description: Abstract Rowhammer is a security vulnerability that allows unauthorized attackers to induce errors within DRAM cells, e.g., to attain elevated user privileges or to extract sensitive information from cryptographic schemes. To prevent fault injections from escalating to successful attacks, a widely accepted mitigation is implementing fault checks on instructions and data.

arxiv-2409-20023.title: CNN-Assisted Particle Swarm Optimization of a Perturbation-Based Model for Nonlinearity Compensation in Optical Transmission Systems
arxiv-2409-20023.creator: Alexey Redyuk, Evgeny Shevelev, Vitaly Danilko, Mikhail Fedoruk
arxiv-2409-20023.description: Abstract Nonlinear signal distortions are one of the primary factors limiting the capacity and reach of optical transmission systems. Currently, several approaches exist for compensating nonlinear distortions, but for practical implementation, algorithms must be simultaneously accurate, fast, and robust against various interferences.

pmc-11679377.title: Resource-Efficient FPGA Architecture for Real-Time RFI Mitigation in Interferometric Radiometers
pmc-11679377.creator: Adrian Perez-Portero, Jorge Querol, Adriano Camps
pmc-11679377.description: Interferometric radiometers operating at L-band, such as ESA’s SMOS mission, enable crucial Earth observations providing high-resolution measurements of soil moisture, ocean salinity, and other geophysical parameters. pmc-13491348.creator: Hao-Wei Lee, Yoshinobu Onuma, Patrick W Serruys
pmc-13491348.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). owever, we would like to raise a methodological consideration regarding the interpretation of “accuracy.”

In the study, microcomputed tomography (μCT)-derived measurements from silicone models were used as the reference standard. Although μCT provides high-resolution imaging and enables 3-dimensional reconstruction, μCT-based measurements are not direct physical ground truth but reconstructed representations subject to segmentation variability, threshold selection, voxel resolution limits, and reconstruction artifacts. Thus, μCT should be considered a high-quality reference modality rather than an absolute standard.
